title: PowerToys Settings window can't open in Windows10

judgment.rationale: The newest activity links a newer open issue with the same Settings-launch failure, making separate implementation work duplicative.
evidence: Issue reports Settings fails to open after a click on Windows 10.
The same issue also has a second Windows 10 reporter, confirming a recurring symptom but not a distinct root cause.
judgment.recommended_action: Post a public deduplication note linking #50335; keep this issue open only if Quick Access proves distinct.

fix_assessment.rationale: A separate PowerToys fix is not justified while the overlapping open report #50335 owns the shared investigation.

issue_context.summary: The report describes Settings and Quick Access failing to open on Windows 10, and the newest comment links the still-open #50335 report with the same Settings symptom.
known_information: Settings and Quick Access both show a brief busy cursor and no visible page.
A PowerToys diagnostic ZIP is attached to the issue.
inferences: #50335 appears to be the current canonical report for the overlapping Settings-launch failure.
The Quick Access symptom may be related but is not proven identical from the public text.
issue_context.analysis: The current open duplicate should own investigation; keeping a separate fix design would risk splitting evidence and maintainer work.
initial_investigation: #50335 is open and was updated after #49011.
The issue history includes another Windows 10 reporter with the same symptom.
Search also found older open/closed Settings-launch reports, but none is a better current owner than #50335.

actions.label: Link to current Settings-launch report
actions.note: Point maintainers and the reporter to the newer overlapping issue rather than starting duplicate implementation work.

comment.body: This report overlaps the still-open #50335, “I can't open powertoys settings by double clicking,” which was updated more recently and covers the same Windows 10 Settings-launch symptom. Please continue the diagnostic discussion and any fix work on #50335 so the Settings and Quick Access evidence stays together; retain this issue only if Quick Access has a distinct failure that #50335 does not cover.
